objectives.text: Run a military-led transition on its own timetable: a referendum on 30 August 2026 on a new constitution that strengthens the presidency (parliament cut from 102 to 65 seats), then presidential and legislative elections on 6 December 2026. The transition charter bars the transitional president and prime minister from standing.

grand_strategy.reading: Guinea-Bissau's strategy is to run a military-led transition on its own timetable, with a presidency strengthened for whoever wins the December vote, in a state too weak to police its own coast. Its outside links are narrow: a suspended ECOWAS seat, a Portuguese channel the junta has just rejected, and a Senegalese neighbour that co-leads the mediation. Gaps: Russia's 2025 contacts, the ECOMIB withdrawal, the Casamance rear (our inference, not sourced here) and any current cashew or cocaine figure are not verified in this pass.

stances.note: ECOWAS suspended Guinea-Bissau from its decision-making bodies after the coup of 26 November 2025, and its mediators (Bio, Faye) then took part in talks with the junta. The junta cooperates in the talks and resists the bloc's terms (a short, structured transition): reluctant_partner is our reading (C); no source uses the words. Trend cooling from the suspension. Bond none is our reading. Gaps: the 2025 withdrawal of the ECOMIB stabilisation force and whether the suspension has been lifted are not verified in this pass.
